title: Exact modular quadratic-mask probabilities and black-box query limits
summary: Useful benchmarks for modular sketches, polynomial-evaluation codes, phase masking, and proposed derandomization or anticoncentration claims.
content: For uniform Boolean quadratic Q and Z=sum_(x in S)(-1)^Q(x) modulo 3, detection probability is (2/3)*(1-(-1/2)^|S|) for 1<=|S|<=7 and for eight-point sets other than affine three-cubes. An affine three-cube has probability 29/64. An alternating-matrix rank recurrence computes the exact probability on every affine d-space; d=5 gives 14509/32768. Separately, K arbitrary F9-valued masks on an N-point universe miss some nonempty subset whenever 4K<N; the F3 threshold is 2K<N. Both are sharp for arbitrary masks.
whenToUse: Useful benchmarks for modular sketches, polynomial-evaluation codes, phase masking, and proposed derandomization or anticoncentration claims.
limitations: No uniform random-detection bound for all subsets is proved. The deterministic lower bound is for arbitrary hidden subsets and black-box queries, not algorithms exploiting succinct input structure. These statements do not provide a fast evaluator.

evidence.details:
Written proofs and exhaustive saved small-case census; affine probabilities through dimension six rechecked during survey.

Written proof means a proof is present in the project and was reviewed for this survey; it does not imply formal verification or established literature novelty. Proposed uses outside this project are transfer suggestions, not demonstrated applications. Scripts are working research prototypes with cross-file imports, not a standalone library.
